title: Resample Your First Beat
blurb: Stack a kick/snare loop, trim it, then layer hats and a melody on top — all inside the unit.

steps.title: Gather your elements
body: Record or load a kick, snare, and hi-hat onto three separate pads — pads 1, 2, and 3 on Bank A.
Have a chopped sample or a melodic phrase ready on another pad, say pad 5.
Play each one to check the levels are roughly even. Resampling prints whatever you hear, so fix balance now rather than later.
steps.checkpoint: Four pads, four sounds, no surprises in volume.
steps.tip: Keep one bank free for your resampled loops so you never overwrite a source sound.

steps.title: Set your metronome and tempo
body: Enter the metronome menu, turn it ON, and set your target tempo.
90 BPM is a classic hip-hop groove and an easy speed to play accurately.
steps.checkpoint: You hear a steady click, and the tempo reads 90.
steps.tip: Start the practice metronome below and tap along on your pads before you record anything. Recording a sloppy take costs more time than practising the bar twice.

steps.title: Lay down the foundation
body: Press RESAMPLE.
Select an empty pad to record onto — pad 9. It starts blinking red.
Hit REC to arm it. Resampling begins the instant audio plays or you hit a pad.
Tap pad 1 (kick) and pad 2 (snare) in time with the metronome for 2 or 4 bars.
Hit REC, or the destination pad, to stop the moment the final bar finishes.
steps.checkpoint: Pad 9 plays back your kick and snare as one sound.
steps.tip: Count yourself in out loud. Stopping one beat late is the most common mistake here, and it shows up as a gap when you loop.

steps.title: Trim and loop it
body: Tap pad 9, then press START/END.
Use CTRL 1 and CTRL 2 to move the start point onto the first kick transient and the end point to exactly where the loop resets.
Press LOOP on pad 9 to test playback.
If it stutters or drifts, nudge the end point until it rolls over seamlessly.
steps.checkpoint: Pad 9 loops indefinitely with no click, gap, or hiccup at the seam.
steps.tip: Trim the start tight to the transient. Even a few milliseconds of silence in front makes every later layer feel late.

steps.title: Layer the hats and melody
body: Press RESAMPLE again and pick a new empty pad — pad 10.
Press REC to arm.
Hit pad 9 to start your drum loop playing, then play pad 3 (hi-hat) and pad 5 (melody) over the top in real time.
Tap REC when the loop finishes to capture the full, layered beat.
steps.checkpoint: Pad 10 is a single pad holding your whole beat: drums, hats, and melody.
steps.tip: Pad 9 still holds the clean drum loop. Keep it — if the layered take is wrong, you re-record pad 10 instead of starting over.

steps.title: Where to go next
body: You now have a one-pad beat and a fallback drum loop, which is the core resampling loop: build, print, layer, repeat.
Each resample pass is committed audio, so work in stages you are happy with rather than one long take.
Try the same process with effects printed in — that is the Bus FX guide — or sequence pad 10 into a longer arrangement with the Pattern Sequencer guide.
steps.tip: Resampling is destructive by nature. Back up your project to an SD card before a big session.
